docs.title: ADF Library for Atlassian Document Format
docs.text: ADF Library is a Python library for building Atlassian Document Format (ADF) JSON documents used by Jira, Confluence, and other Atlassian Cloud products.

docs.title: Why use this library?
docs.text:
• Build ADF documents with Python instead of hand-writing JSON
  • Use focused helpers for common content such as Text, Table, and Link
  • Use generic Node and Mark builders for the latest published ADF node and mark types
  • Export plain dictionaries that can be sent directly to Atlassian APIs

docs.title: Who is this for?
docs.text: This project is for Python developers integrating with Atlassian APIs, automation scripts, issue creation workflows, and content migration pipelines.

docs.title: What does it support?
docs.text:
The library supports:

  • headings, paragraphs, tables, and links through dedicated helpers
  • latest-schema ADF nodes such as lists, panels, code blocks, cards, media, layout, status, and expands through Node
  • latest-schema ADF marks such as backgroundColor, annotation, alignment, textColor, and link

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from adf_lib import ADF, Node, NodeType, Text

doc = ADF()
doc.add(Text("Incident Summary").heading())
doc.add(
    Node(
        NodeType.BULLET_LIST,
        content=[
            Node(
                NodeType.LIST_ITEM,
                content=[
                    Node(
                        NodeType.PARAGRAPH,
                        content=[Node(NodeType.TEXT, text="Service restored")],
                    )
                ],
            )
        ],
    )
)

docs.title: Can I use this for Jira and Confluence?
docs.text: Yes. The library generates Atlassian Document Format structures that can be used with Atlassian Cloud APIs where ADF is accepted.

docs.title: How do I build nodes not covered by helper classes?
docs.text: Use Node with a NodeType value and optional attrs, content, text, or marks.

docs.title: Where can I verify the schema?
docs.text:
See the official Atlassian ADF documentation and schema:

  • https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/
  • http://go.atlassian.com/adf-json-schema

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before installing the ADF Library, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

docs.title: Python Environment
docs.text:
• Python (3.8 or higher recommended)
  • pip package manager

docs.title: Method 1: Using pip (Recommended)
docs.text: pip install adf_lib

docs.title: Method 2: From Source
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/username/adf_lib.git
  1. Navigate to the directory:
cd adf_lib
  1. Install using pip:
pip install .

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Verify the installation by checking the version:

pip show adf_lib

Or in Python:

import adf_lib
print(adf_lib.__version__)

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
To upgrade to the latest version:

pip install --upgrade adf_lib

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text:
To remove the package:

pip uninstall adf_lib

docs.title: Permission Errors
docs.text:
If you encounter permission errors:

# Windows (Run as Administrator)
pip install adf_lib --user

# Linux/macOS
sudo pip install adf_lib

docs.title: SSL Certificate Errors
docs.text:
If you face SSL certificate issues:

pip install --trusted-host pypi.org --trusted-host files.pythonhosted.org adf_lib

docs.title: Package Conflicts
docs.text:
If you experience dependency conflicts:

pip install adf_lib --ignore-installed

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: ADF Library helps you create Atlassian Document Format (ADF) documents for Jira and Confluence with Python.

docs.title: Import the core components
docs.text:
from adf_lib import ADF, Link, Mark, Node, NodeType, Table, Text
from adf_lib.constants.enums import HeadingLevel

docs.title: Create a document
docs.text: doc = ADF()

docs.title: Add headings and paragraphs
docs.text:
doc.add(Text("My Document").heading(HeadingLevel.H1))
doc.add(Text("This is a paragraph").paragraph())
doc.add(Text("Bold and italic", "strong", "em").paragraph())

docs.title: Add links
docs.text:
link = Link(href="https://example.com", title="Example")
doc.add(Text("Open example", link.to_mark()).paragraph())

docs.title: Add a table
docs.text:
table = Table(width=100)
table.add_row(
    [
        table.header([Text("Name").paragraph()]),
        table.header([Text("Status").paragraph()]),
    ]
)
table.add_row(
    [
        table.cell([Text("Search indexing").paragraph()]),
        table.cell([Text("Healthy").paragraph()]),
    ]
)
doc.add(table.to_dict())

docs.title: Use the latest ADF nodes
docs.text:
doc.add(
    Node(
        NodeType.PANEL,
        attrs={"panelType": "info"},
        content=[Text("Deployment completed").paragraph()],
    )
)

doc.add(
    Node(
        NodeType.PARAGRAPH,
        content=[
            Node(
                NodeType.TEXT,
                text="Highlighted",
                marks=[Mark("backgroundColor", {"color": "#FFFAE6"})],
            )
        ],
    )
)

docs.title: Export to a dictionary
docs.text: adf_dict = doc.to_dict()

docs.title: Document Structure
docs.text:
ADF documents are hierarchical JSON objects with a root doc node, a version, and a content array.

{
    "version": 1,
    "type": "doc",
    "content": [
        # child nodes
    ]
}

docs.title: Core helpers
docs.text:
The library includes dedicated helpers for common ADF authoring:

class ContentType(Enum):
    TEXT = "text"
    TABLE = "table"

docs.title: Latest node coverage
docs.text:
For the latest published ADF schema, use NodeType with the generic Node builder.

class NodeType(Enum):
    PARAGRAPH = "paragraph"
    HEADING = "heading"
    BULLET_LIST = "bulletList"
    ORDERED_LIST = "orderedList"
    LIST_ITEM = "listItem"
    CODE_BLOCK = "codeBlock"
    PANEL = "panel"
    BLOCKQUOTE = "blockquote"
    RULE = "rule"
    HARD_BREAK = "hardBreak"
    # ... plus cards, media, layout, task, decision, and extension nodes

docs.title: Text helper
docs.text:
class Text:
    def __init__(self, text: str, *marks: Union[str, dict, Mark])
    def heading(self, level: Union[int, HeadingLevel] = HeadingLevel.H1,
                local_id: Optional[str] = None) -> dict
    def paragraph(self, local_id: Optional[str] = None) -> dict

docs.title: Generic node helper
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Node:
    type: Union[str, NodeType]
    attrs: Optional[dict] = None
    content: Optional[List[Union[dict, Node, Table]]] = None
    text: Optional[str] = None
    marks: List[Union[str, dict, Mark]] = field(default_factory=list)

Use Node for:

  • lists
  • cards
  • panels
  • status and date nodes
  • layout and media nodes
  • extension and expand nodes

Pass child content as:

  • ADF dictionaries
  • Node instances
  • Table instances

If you are using Text, first convert it with .paragraph() or .heading(). Those helper methods return ADF dictionaries, which are valid content items.

docs.title: Mark coverage
docs.text:
The library supports the existing text marks plus latest-schema marks through MarkType and Mark.

class MarkType(Enum):
    ALIGNMENT = "alignment"
    ANNOTATION = "annotation"
    BACKGROUND_COLOR = "backgroundColor"
    CODE = "code"
    EM = "em"
    LINK = "link"
    STRIKE = "strike"
    STRONG = "strong"
    SUBSUP = "subsup"
    TEXT_COLOR = "textColor"
    UNDERLINE = "underline"

docs.title: Build common ADF content
docs.text:
from adf_lib import ADF, Link, Table, Text

doc = ADF()
doc.add(Text("Weekly Update").heading())
doc.add(Text("Everything looks healthy.").paragraph())

link = Link(href="https://status.example.com", title="Status page")
doc.add(Text("Open the status page", link.to_mark()).paragraph())

table = Table(width=100)
table.add_row(
    [
        table.header([Text("Service").paragraph()]),
        table.header([Text("State").paragraph()]),
    ]
)
table.add_row(
    [
        table.cell([Text("Search").paragraph()]),
        table.cell([Text("Operational").paragraph()]),
    ]
)
doc.add(table.to_dict())

docs.title: Build newer schema nodes with Node
docs.text:
from adf_lib import Mark, Node, NodeType, Text

panel = Node(
    NodeType.PANEL,
    attrs={"panelType": "note"},
    content=[Text("Remember to rotate the credentials.").paragraph()],
)

bullet_list = Node(
    NodeType.BULLET_LIST,
    content=[
        Node(
            NodeType.LIST_ITEM,
            content=[
                Node(
                    NodeType.PARAGRAPH,
                    content=[Node(NodeType.TEXT, text="Create the change request")],
                )
            ],
        ),
        Node(
            NodeType.LIST_ITEM,
            content=[
                Node(
                    NodeType.PARAGRAPH,
                    content=[Node(NodeType.TEXT, text="Validate the deployment")],
                )
            ],
        ),
    ],
)

highlighted_text = Node(
    NodeType.TEXT,
    text="Needs follow up",
    marks=[Mark("backgroundColor", {"color": "#FFFAE6"})],
)

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: We are committed to providing a friendly, welcoming, and inclusive environment for all contributors to this project. By participating in this project, you agree to abide by this code of conduct.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
We appreciate your contributions! To help you get started, here are the steps you can follow:

  1. Fork the repository Fork the repository to your personal GitHub account to make changes.

  2. Create a new branch Always create a new branch for your work, whether you're fixing a bug, adding a new feature, or updating documentation.

  3. Make your changes Implement your changes, keeping the code clean, well-organized, and following any existing patterns and style guidelines.

  4. Commit your changes Write clear, concise commit messages that describe what you've done. Use the present tense (e.g., "Fix bug" rather than "Fixed bug").

  5. Push your changes to your fork Push the changes to your personal fork on GitHub.

  6. Create a pull request Once you're ready, open a pull request to propose your changes. Make sure your pull request follows the guidelines below:

  7. Write tests: Add relevant unit tests to cover your changes. Unit tests are an essential part of our process and help ensure stability and correctness.

  8. Do developer testing: Before submitting your pull request, thoroughly test your changes in the development environment.

  9. Update documentation: If your changes affect functionality or introduce new features, please update the documentation accordingly to reflect those changes.

docs.title: Additional Guidelines
docs.text:
• Respect others: Treat all participants with kindness, respect, and empathy. We foster a collaborative and inclusive community.

  • Be open to feedback: Code reviews are a valuable process for improving the quality of the project. Be open to suggestions and critique.

  • No harassment: Harassment, offensive behavior, and discrimination are not tolerated. If you witness or experience inappropriate conduct, please report it immediately.

By following these guidelines, we can maintain a productive and positive environment for all contributors.

Thank you for contributing to our project!
